title: Riptide - Collection Health
description: Is flow collection healthy right now — is every exporter delivering? Status wall for the operator running the Riptide collector: verdict on top, fleet activity and collection lag below, inventory with drill-down at the bottom. All panels read ingest time (receivedAt), not flow switch time, so they measure the collection pipeline rather than the traffic.

panels.title: Exporters reporting — last 15 min
panels.description: Distinct exporters that delivered at least one flow record in the last 15 minutes, independent of the selected time range. Normal: matches the number of devices configured to export to this collector. NONE (red) means the collector is receiving nothing — check the collector first: is the container up, is /readyz returning 200, is UDP 9999 reachable? See the operations runbook linked in the dashboard header.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT uniqExact(exporterAddr) AS "Exporters reporting"
FROM ${database}.flows
WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 DAY AND receivedAt >= now() - INTERVAL 15 MINUTE AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)

panels.title: Silent exporters — seen in range, quiet 15 min
panels.description: Exporters that delivered flows inside the selected time range but nothing in its final 15 minutes (relative to the range end, so panning into the past judges that window, not now). Normal: 0 (green). Any other value (red) means a device stopped exporting or its packets stopped arriving — check the exporter device and the network path to the collector before suspecting the collector itself, since the other exporters are still getting through. On a quiet network with genuinely idle exporters, widen the mental threshold accordingly; ranges shorter than 15 minutes make this panel meaningless.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT countIf(lastSeen < $__toTime - INTERVAL 15 MINUTE) AS "Silent exporters"
FROM (
  SELECT exporterAddr, max(receivedAt) AS lastSeen
  FROM ${database}.flows
  WHERE $__timeFilter(timestamp) AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)
  GROUP BY exporterAddr
)

panels.title: Flow record rate — last 5 min
panels.description: Flow records received per second, averaged over the last 5 minutes, independent of the selected time range. Normal: steady and roughly proportional to network activity; compare against the 'Flow records by exporter' panel below for what steady looks like here. STALLED (red) means zero records arrived in 5 minutes — treat it like 'Exporters reporting = NONE' and start with the collector's /readyz and the UDP listener port.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT count() / 300 AS "Flow record rate"
FROM ${database}.flows
WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 DAY AND receivedAt >= now() - INTERVAL 5 MINUTE AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)

panels.title: Collection lag p95 — last 15 min
panels.description: 95th percentile of the delay between a flow ending on the exporter (lastSwitched) and the record arriving at the collector (receivedAt), over the last 15 minutes. Normal: seconds to about a minute, dominated by the exporter's active/inactive timeout settings. Amber above 1 minute, red above 5: sustained high lag means export batching delay, a congested path to the collector, or exporter clock skew (the collector records the skew it corrects in the clockCorrection column). Flows that end after their receipt are left out here and counted in "Flows ending after their receipt" below: a negative lag is not a fast collector.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT if(countIf(receivedAt >= lastSwitched) > 0, quantileIf(0.95)(dateDiff('millisecond', lastSwitched, receivedAt), receivedAt >= lastSwitched) / 1000, NULL) AS "Collection lag p95"
FROM ${database}.flows
WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 DAY AND receivedAt >= now() - INTERVAL 15 MINUTE AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)

panels.title: Lost in riptide — last 15 min
panels.description: Flows riptide received but did not store in the last 15 minutes: socket drops, dispatch drops and errors, dropped and failed batch rows (riptide:lost_total from riptide-alerts.yml), and flow sets it could not decode because it held no template for them. Every other tile on this dashboard reads ClickHouse and so only sees flows that arrived; this is the one that sees the ones that did not. Normal is 0. Anything else: open Riptide - Health, which names the stage. It covers the whole collector: riptide's own metrics carry no tenant or zone, so the Tenant and Zone filters do not apply to it. "No data" means the chosen Prometheus lacks riptide's recording rules or does not scrape riptide as job="riptide", not that nothing was lost.

links.title: Riptide - Health: which stage is losing flows

panels.title: Exporters delivering — per interval
panels.description: How many exporters delivered at least one flow in each interval, by ingest time. A flat line is a healthy fleet; a dip is exporters going silent, and the exporter inventory below names them (sorted by "Silent for"). Replaces a per-exporter timeline, which cannot show a fleet of thousands. Only complete intervals are drawn.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT toStartOfInterval(receivedAt, toIntervalSecond($__interval_s)) AS time,
       uniqExact(exporterAddr) AS "Exporters delivering"
FROM ${database}.flows
WHERE $__timeFilter(receivedAt) AND receivedAt < toStartOfInterval($__toTime, toIntervalSecond($__interval_s)) AND timestamp >= $__fromTime - INTERVAL 1 DAY AND timestamp <= $__toTime + INTERVAL 1 DAY AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Flow records by exporter
panels.description: Flow records received per second, stacked by exporter (top 10 by record count, remainder as Other), bucketed by ingest time. Normal: each exporter contributes a steady band. To find which exporter went silent, read the "Silent for" column of the exporter inventory below. Only complete intervals are drawn, so the right edge never shows a partial interval as a drop.

targets.rawSql:
WITH top AS (SELECT exporterAddr AS dim FROM ${database}.flows WHERE $__timeFilter(timestamp) AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone) GROUP BY dim ORDER BY count() DESC LIMIT 10)
SELECT toStartOfInterval(receivedAt, toIntervalSecond($__interval_s)) AS time,
       if(exporterAddr IN (SELECT dim FROM top), if(exporterName != '', exporterName, exporterAddr), 'Other') AS series,
       count() / $__interval_s AS rate
FROM ${database}.flows
WHERE $__timeFilter(receivedAt) AND receivedAt < toStartOfInterval($__toTime, toIntervalSecond($__interval_s)) AND timestamp >= $__fromTime - INTERVAL 1 DAY AND timestamp <= $__toTime + INTERVAL 1 DAY AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)
GROUP BY time, series
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Flow records by protocol
panels.description: Flow records received per second, stacked by flow protocol (NetFlow v5/v9, IPFIX, sFlow), bucketed by ingest time. Normal: the mix is stable — each device exports one protocol, so this is the exporter fleet seen by protocol. A protocol band vanishing means every exporter of that type stopped at once, which points at a shared cause: a template/parsing problem on the collector for that protocol, or a shared network path. Only complete intervals are drawn, so the right edge never shows a partial interval as a drop.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT toStartOfInterval(receivedAt, toIntervalSecond($__interval_s)) AS time,
       toString(flowProtocol) AS series,
       count() / $__interval_s AS rate
FROM ${database}.flows
WHERE $__timeFilter(receivedAt) AND receivedAt < toStartOfInterval($__toTime, toIntervalSecond($__interval_s)) AND timestamp >= $__fromTime - INTERVAL 1 DAY AND timestamp <= $__toTime + INTERVAL 1 DAY AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)
GROUP BY time, series
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Collection lag over time — p50 / p95
panels.description: Median and 95th-percentile delay between a flow ending on the exporter (lastSwitched) and its record arriving at the collector (receivedAt), per bucket. Normal: flat, seconds to about a minute, set by the exporters' active/inactive timeouts; p95 well above p50 means a subset of exporters lags behind the rest. A step change in both percentiles is a configuration or clock event — compare with the per-exporter panels to see whether one exporter or all of them moved. Only complete intervals are drawn, so the right edge never shows a partial interval as a drop. Flows with an end time after their receipt are left out; they are the "Flows ending after their receipt" panel.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT toStartOfInterval(receivedAt, toIntervalSecond($__interval_s)) AS time,
       quantileIf(0.5)(dateDiff('millisecond', lastSwitched, receivedAt), receivedAt >= lastSwitched) / 1000 AS "p50",
       quantileIf(0.95)(dateDiff('millisecond', lastSwitched, receivedAt), receivedAt >= lastSwitched) / 1000 AS "p95"
FROM ${database}.flows
WHERE $__timeFilter(receivedAt) AND receivedAt < toStartOfInterval($__toTime, toIntervalSecond($__interval_s)) AND timestamp >= $__fromTime - INTERVAL 1 DAY AND timestamp <= $__toTime + INTERVAL 1 DAY AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Flows ending after their receipt — share
panels.description: The share of flows whose end time (lastSwitched) is later than the moment riptide received them. An exporter clock running ahead of riptide's does this, and so does an exporter that reports end times in the future: with nl6 v0.32.0 and every clock NTP-synchronized, about 89 % of flows ended some 2 minutes after receipt, alike for NetFlow v5, v9 and IPFIX. Their lag is meaningless, so the lag panels leave them out. Normal is 0 %. A steady share points at one exporter or a fleet: check its clock first, then Riptide - Data Trust for the clock corrections riptide applied.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT toStartOfInterval(receivedAt, toIntervalSecond($__interval_s)) AS time,
       countIf(lastSwitched > receivedAt) / count() * 100 AS "ending after receipt"
FROM ${database}.flows
WHERE $__timeFilter(receivedAt) AND receivedAt < toStartOfInterval($__toTime, toIntervalSecond($__interval_s)) AND timestamp >= $__fromTime - INTERVAL 1 DAY AND timestamp <= $__toTime + INTERVAL 1 DAY AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)
GROUP BY time
ORDER BY time

panels.title: Exporter inventory — last seen, volume, drill-down
panels.description: Every exporter seen in the selected range: name (address where unnamed), protocols spoken, tenants and zones it feeds, when its last record arrived, how long it has been silent (background turns red past 15 minutes), and what it delivered. Sorted silent-first so the problem row is on top. Click an exporter name to open Flow Forensics scoped to that exporter with the current filters and time range — from there, slice by host, port, protocol or application.

value.title: Slice flows for this exporter (Flow Forensics)

targets.rawSql:
SELECT if(max(exporterName) != '', max(exporterName), exporterAddr) AS "Exporter",
       exporterAddr AS "Address",
       arrayStringConcat(groupUniqArray(toString(flowProtocol)), ', ') AS "Protocols",
       arrayStringConcat(groupUniqArray(tenant), ', ') AS "Tenants",
       arrayStringConcat(groupUniqArray(zone), ', ') AS "Zones",
       max(receivedAt) AS "Last seen",
       dateDiff('second', max(receivedAt), $__toTime) AS "Silent for",
       count() AS "Records",
       sum(bytes) AS "Volume"
FROM ${database}.flows
WHERE $__timeFilter(timestamp) AND $__conditionalAll(tenant IN (${tenant:singlequote}), $tenant) AND $__conditionalAll(zone IN (${zone:singlequote}), $zone)
GROUP BY exporterAddr
ORDER BY "Silent for" DESC
